chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya and others, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Ibn al-Tayyar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Indeed, God has argued against the people with what He gave them and made known to them.
Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj — similar to it.

key_terms.آتاهم: What He gave them; referring to reason, prophetic guidance, and innate knowledge (fitra)
key_terms.احتجّ: Argued/established proof; a technical theological term meaning God made His case against humanity by providing them with the means of guidance
key_terms.الحجة: The proof/argument; a core concept in Shia theology referring to God's conclusive evidence upon creation
key_terms.عرّفهم: Made known to them; referring to God's revelation and making knowledge accessible

ai.seo_question: What is God's proof (hujja) upon humanity according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) states that God's proof (hujja) upon humanity is established through His own gifts and revelations — namely, the innate knowledge (fitra), intellectual capacity, and prophetic guidance He has bestowed. This doctrine of divine proof is central to Shia theology of imamate, affirming that God does not hold people accountable beyond what He has made accessible to them through reason and revelation.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, and someone else, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj, from Ibn Al Tayyar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Argued upon the people with what He<sup>azwj</sup> Gave them and Introduced them (to)’.
Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazan, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj – similar to it.
